threads.body: `BasicDataSource.getConnection()` delegates to `createDataSource().getConnection()`, so this advice runs on **every** connection acquisition, not just once at pool creation. For an unnamed data source, `DataSourceMetrics.getDefaultName()` therefore advances the shared `idGenerator` counter on each `getConnection()` call, even though `registerMetrics()` already registered the pool under the first generated name (it uses `computeIfAbsent`, so later names are discarded). The previous fallback used `System.identityHashCode(dataSource)`, which was stable across repeated calls; the new counter both leaks IDs (unbounded growth for a busy unnamed pool) and makes the generated `dbcp2-N` numbering non-deterministic. Consider resolving/generating the default name only when the data source is not already registered (e.g. compute the name lazily inside `registerMetrics`).

`getDefaultName()` is only used by the javaagent fallback path — the library's manual registration entrypoint (`ApacheDbcpTelemetry.registerMetrics`) requires callers to supply an explicit name, as noted in the PR description. Making `DataSourceMetrics` `public` and exposing `getDefaultName()` adds it to this library module's stable public API, committing the project to maintaining it. The analogous javaagent-only helper in the hbase module (`OpenTelemetryCallUtil`) keeps its static state inside the javaagent module rather than in the library API. Consider hosting the default-name counter in the javaagent module (e.g. a javaagent helper class) and keeping `DataSourceMetrics` package-private.

> I don't think we should provide uniqueness here. It's a nice idea, but I think worse to have inconsistent numbers between restarts than to have merged into one metric (but consistent).

@trask  When multiple DataSources are used without assigned names, the previous naming scheme "dbcp2-" + System.identityHashCode(dataSource) can still expose metrics after service restarts even though the suffix value changes.
I acknowledge that this approach causes the identifier to shift from dbcp2-1 to dbcp2-2 after restarts, yet I do not consider this the worst-case outcome.
By contrast, your proposal to hardcode the fixed value apache-dbcp2 introduces two critical drawbacks:
While the original implementation suffered from high cardinality, it guaranteed metric exposure for all multiple DataSource instances. If we switch to the static apache-dbcp2 label, metrics from DataSource1 will be overwritten by those from DataSource2 after restarts, which I argue creates a far worse problem.
As core application metrics, connection pool indicators are far more valuable to retain than to eliminate entirely. Even with fluctuating metric names, operators can distinguish different DataSources via attributes such as maximum connection limit.
In the worst case, application maintainers can map metrics to specific DataSource definitions by cross-referencing auxiliary signals like request volume metrics, and proactively standardize explicit DataSource naming on their own initiative.
The fundamental motivation behind migrating away from the System.identityHashCode(dataSource) high-cardinality strategy is to reduce excessive pressure on time-series storage and metric query engines.

Relevant context from [opentelemetry-java#7264](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java/pull/7264):

Before that PR, `AsynchronousMetricStorage` stored one point per attribute set. If another callback reported the same attributes during collection, the SDK logged `has recorded multiple values for the same attributes` and dropped the later observation.

#7264 added spatial aggregation for asynchronous instruments, primarily so observations that collapse to the same attributes after view filtering are properly reaggregated. It replaced the point map and duplicate-warning/drop branch with aggregation handles keyed by the processed attributes.

The result depends on the instrument's aggregation. For these DBCP observable up/down counters, the aggregation is `Sum`, so observations from pools sharing the same `pool.name` are added into one series. No duplicate-observation warning is emitted. This change was released in OpenTelemetry Java 1.50.0, while this repository uses 1.63.0.

Ideally connection pools would have unique names that allow identifying which pool given metrics apply to. If the pools don't have names and we add a sequence number then from user perspective it might not be possible to tell which pool these metrics apply to unless there is something else that allows distinguishing the pools e.g. one pool has a larger max value. Further more if there is some sort of ambiguity in initialization order then poole names from different nodes could be swapped. Also note that the sequencing as implemented in this PR is per application. If the same node deploys more than 1 application that uses the connection pool these would still get the same name. I also think that not adding the sequence number might be better.

Ideally, assigning a unique name to each connection pool would be the optimal approach. However, I have extracted statistical data from several of our applications and found that the vast majority do not configure a dedicated name for their connection pools. The previous implementation, despite its high cardinality issue, was capable of exporting two metrics. If we replace it with a fixed value, only one metric can be exposed, which will inevitably bring negative impacts to end users.

My proposal is to adopt a compromised solution that enables users to keep using the service normally without any code or configuration changes. This can minimize disruption to users while eliminating the high cardinality problem entirely.

It is unreliable to distinguish connection pools by parameters such as the maximum number of connections, as this cannot resolve the fundamental root cause. Therefore, I personally advise against this method.

I acknowledge that deploying two instances belonging to different applications on the same host node will result in identical default pool names. We can differentiate metrics during storage by appending the application identifier, which I believe is a completely viable solution. The core objective of this revision is not to generate distinct default connection pool names across different applications. On the contrary, reusing the same default name among various applications helps reduce the cardinality overhead in time-series storage.

Our plan is to apply a fixed string as the connection pool name when users do not explicitly specify one. For connection pool frameworks including HikariCP and Vibur-DBCP, the default behavior is to generate pool names via auto-increment IDs. Should we add mandatory logic to override these auto-generated names? If we skip this modification, different connection pool components will behave inconsistently when no custom pool name is configured, leading to a poor unified user experience.

@trask @laurit Could you two please conduct a follow-up evaluation? Kindly let me know if we still stick to the rule of using a fixed value as the connection pool name whenever no custom name is specified. If this scheme is confirmed, I will proceed with relevant code adjustments accordingly.

From https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/db/#db-client-connection-pool-name:

> The name of the connection pool; unique within the instrumented application. In case the connection pool implementation doesn't provide a name, instrumentation SHOULD use a combination of parameters that would make the name unique, for example, combining attributes `server.address`, `server.port`, and `db.namespace`, formatted as `server.address:server.port/db.namespace`. Instrumentations that generate connection pool name following different patterns SHOULD document it.

Some other things we could consider:

| Identity source | Possible for Apache DBCP 2? | Availability and implementation | Stability and cardinality | Limitations and recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Explicit `BasicDataSource.getJmxName()` | Yes; directly supported since DBCP 2.0 | Read `getJmxName()` when the underlying pool starts. No JMX registration is required for the configured value to be available. If it is a valid JMX `ObjectName`, the `name` key could be extracted; otherwise preserve the configured value. | Stable across restarts and nodes when configuration is consistent. Cardinality is controlled by the application. | Best signal and highest priority. A value configured after metrics registration would require unregistering and re-registering the metric callback. |
| Registered JMX `ObjectName` | Yes; implemented by the current PR | `getRegisteredJmxName()` is protected. An injected helper in `org.apache.commons.dbcp2` can access it and extract its `name` key, falling back to the complete `ObjectName`. | Usually stable because it comes from container or deployment configuration. Cardinality is bounded by registered pools. | Only available after registration. If the DBCP pool starts before JMX registration, the instrumentation must either update the metric registration later from `preRegister()` or retain the earlier fallback. |
| Spring bean name | Yes, but requires Spring instrumentation | DBCP does not know its Spring bean name. Instrument Spring's bean initialization lifecycle, such as `AbstractAutowireCapableBeanFactory.initializeBean(beanName, bean, ...)`, and publish the name to a shared weak identity or `VirtualField` registry. The DBCP instrumentation reads that registry at pool startup. | Stable, meaningful, and bounded by the application's bean definitions. Normally consistent across nodes. | A datasource may be started inside an `@Bean` factory method before Spring associates the returned object with its bean name. Supporting that case requires late metric renaming. The existing Spring `DataSourcePostProcessor` demonstrates that the name is available, but it belongs to the Spring starter path rather than the generic javaagent DBCP module. |
| JNDI resource name | Yes for common DBCP factory creation paths | Instrument `BasicDataSourceFactory.getObjectInstance(..., Name name, ...)` and associate the returned `BasicDataSource` with `name.toString()`. Store it in the same shared identity registry. | Normally stable and operator-friendly, for example `java:comp/env/jdbc/orders`. Cardinality is bounded by configured resources. | The `Name` argument may be absent, and containers can create or bind datasources through other paths. Tomcat's relocated `org.apache.tomcat.dbcp.dbcp2` classes are not covered by instrumentation matching `org.apache.commons.dbcp2.BasicDataSource`. |
| Parsed JDBC target (`host:port/database`) | Yes; strongest self-contained fallback | `BasicDataSource.getUrl()` is public in DBCP 2.0. A same-package helper can also read package-private connection properties when needed. Refactor or expose the existing JDBC URL parser, then construct the name only from `DbInfo.getServerAddress()`, `getServerPort()`, and `getDbNamespace()`. Never include the raw URL, username, password, or query parameters. | Stable across restarts and nodes when connection configuration is stable. Cardinality reflects actual database targets rather than object instances. | Two pools can target the same database, and some JDBC URLs are multi-host, indirect, or unparseable. The existing parser is internal to JDBC instrumentation, so clean reuse requires extracting a shared database-endpoint parser instead of coupling DBCP directly to the JDBC implementation module. |
| Construction-site fingerprint | Yes; useful to disambiguate identical JDBC targets | Instrument the `BasicDataSource` constructor, capture the first application frame after excluding JDK, DBCP, OpenTelemetry, and known framework frames, and store a normalized `class#method` identity in a `VirtualField`. Combine it with the parsed JDBC target. Java 8 can use `new Throwable().getStackTrace()`. | Stable across restarts and nodes while the construction method remains unchanged. Cardinality is bounded by construction sites rather than object instances. | Framework reflection can obscure the application frame. Class or method refactoring changes the name; line numbers should be avoided because unrelated edits move them. Multiple pools created by one method still need a site-local ordinal or another differentiator. Class and method names may expose internal implementation details. |

threads.body: Connection-pool instrumentations in this repo typically set `inline = false` on Byte Buddy advices to avoid inlining agent code into the instrumented library class (e.g., c3p0 and vibur-DBCP datasource advices). Consider restoring `inline = false` here for consistency and to reduce classloading/bytecode footprint in the target method.

For cleanup hooks on `close()`, other connection-pool instrumentations run the unregister advice even when the method throws (via `onThrowable = Throwable.class`) and also keep `inline = false`. Without `onThrowable`, an exception from `close()` can leave the BatchCallback registered and continue emitting metrics.

replies.body: `inline = false` isolates this module's helper classes in a separate classloader. The Apache DBCP helper must access non-public `BasicDataSource` methods, which is not allowed across classloaders even when the package name is the same. This causes `IllegalAccessError` and metrics registration is silently skipped.

threads.body: [General] Matching `postDeregister` still makes metric collection depend on the JMX lifecycle. `postDeregister` signals removal of the MBean, not closure of the connection pool, so a running pool that is temporarily registered and then deregistered loses its callback here. Because `startPoolMaintenance()` has already completed and there is no registration hook left, metrics never resume for that pool. Unregister on `close()` only (or explicitly restore registration for an open pool), and cover deregistration of a still-running pool with a regression test.

[General] The lifecycle paragraph doesn't cover the new `preRegister` path. On DBCP 2.0, a configured `jmxName` makes `createDataSource()` register the MBean before pool creation, so `PreRegisterAdvice` registers metrics *before* `startPoolMaintenance()`. Independently, registering a `BasicDataSource` as an MBean after pool startup unregisters and re-registers the callback, changing `pool.name` from the URL-derived value to the `ObjectName`-derived one (which is what `shouldUpdateDataSourceNameWhenMBeanIsRegisteredAfterPoolStart` covers).

```suggestion
This auto-instrumentation registers metrics when the connection pool is initialized
(`BasicDataSource.startPoolMaintenance()`) or when `BasicDataSource.preRegister(...)` is invoked
during MBean registration, whichever comes first, and unregisters them when the `BasicDataSource`
is closed. JMX registration is not required. When a JMX `ObjectName` is available, its `name`
property is used as the pool name; if the property is absent, the full `ObjectName` is used.
Otherwise, the JDBC URL and connection properties are used to derive
`server.address[:server.port][/db.namespace]`. If neither server address nor database namespace is
available, `apache-dbcp2` is used. A pool registered as an MBean after it has already started
switches from the derived name to the `ObjectName`-based name.
```

The same paragraph in `instrumentation/apache-dbcp-2.0/metadata.yaml` needs the corresponding update.
